clue.text: A fact isn't treated as very odd

indicators.note: letters that are treated are processed or worked on, so these words get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A claim about something being processed as bizarre, or a fact being handled as if it were not one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges the nine letters of A FACT ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic means weird or bizarre, beyond belief, so it can stand for very odd.

clue.text: Having lots of money from a poker hand?

definitions.meaning: a rich person is said to have plenty of cash in hand, well off
in poker, five cards all of the same suit

explanation.surface: A gambler made rich by a good hand at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means well supplied with cash, and is also a poker hand of five cards in one suit.

clue.text: Turn one out, though it's free of charge

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Produce one item even though it costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free of charge' suggests costing nothing; it means electrically uncharged. 'out' rearranges TURN ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle in the atomic nucleus carries no electric charge, unlike the proton.

clue.text: Where all men are brothers?

parts.note: in a monastery the monks address each other as Brother

explanation.surface: A question about a utopia of universal brotherhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all men are brothers' sounds like an ideal of fellowship, but means monks living together.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is home to monks, who are called brothers in their religious community.

clue.text: He may be a master of form

definitions.text: He may be a master of form

parts.words: He may be a master of form
parts.note: a schoolmaster in charge of a form, the British word for a school class

explanation.surface: Someone who is an expert at shape or style, or at racing form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master of form' suggests skill in style, but form is a British school class, and master a schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster instructs pupils, and a form master runs a class in a British school.

clue.text: A charge will be made for this case

definitions.text: A charge will be made for this case

parts.words: A charge will be made for this case
parts.note: a gun's charge of explosive is packed into a casing that holds it

explanation.surface: A lawyer or tradesman warning that a fee will be billed for this job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' and 'case' sound legal or commercial; here a charge is gunpowder and the case holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A casing containing a bullet's propellant charge is the unit loaded into a firearm.

clue.text: Match's quiet atmosphere

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for playing quietly
the atmosphere is the air around us

explanation.surface: A sports report noting the hushed mood at a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' reads as a sporting fixture but is a verb or noun meaning a matching couple; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that match form a matched couple, as with a set of socks or gloves.

clue.text: Fancy a movie?

definitions.meaning: to fancy something is to imagine it, to see it in the mind's eye
a film, as in going to the ...

explanation.surface: An invitation: would you like to see a film?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to imagine, as fancy does, and is also an informal word for a film.

clue.text: Complete tool

definitions.meaning: to complete a plan is to carry it out, put it into effect
a utensil or instrument used for a job

explanation.surface: A full set of equipment, as in a complete toolkit.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to carry out or fulfil; as a noun it is a tool or instrument.

clue.text: It's out of town and out of the country

definitions.text: It's out of town and out of the country

parts.words: It's out of town and out of the country
parts.note: residential outskirts lie beyond the town centre yet are not rural countryside either

explanation.surface: A riddle about somewhere that is neither in the city nor in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the country' suggests going abroad, but here it means not in the rural countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The residential districts on a city's edge are outside the town centre but short of rural land.

clue.text: Crêpe one cooked — instructions provided

indicators.note: something cooked is altered or worked over, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, a thin pancake
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A pancake made, with the method supplied alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges CREPE plus I; 'provided' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of cooking directions telling you how to make a dish is exactly what instructions in a cookbook are.

clue.text: Drink sounds dear to the French

indicators.note: the clue says what follows is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: chérie is the French word for darling or dear

explanation.surface: A drink whose name is pleasing to French people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' signals that the French term of endearment chérie is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from Jerez in Spain is a classic drink, often served as an aperitif.

clue.text: M Poirot has a point — a strong one

parts.note: Agatha Christie's Belgian detective Monsieur Poirot has the first name Hercule
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The detective Poirot makes a sharp observation, a forceful one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a point' looks like Poirot making an argument; it adds a compass point to his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero of legendary strength, so his name is used for any very strong man.

clue.text: Be about to manage one part of Borneo

indicators.note: the word Be goes about, that is around, the manage synonym

parts.note: taken as written
to run something is to manage it
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Instructions to be ready to run a single section of a large island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manage' reads as coping, but gives the verb for running a business; 'about' wraps the clue's first word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: This small sultanate lies on the north coast of the island of Borneo, sharing it with Malaysia and Indonesia.

clue.text: Kick up a fuss, as Adam and Eve did

definitions.meaning: an idiom for causing an uproar or loud protest
Adam and Eve brought up their son Cain, the first child in Genesis

explanation.surface: Our first parents caused trouble, a tale of the Garden of Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick up a fuss' is the idiom; the second sense takes the words literally, since Adam and Eve reared Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a great commotion, and literally describes bringing up the biblical son of Adam and Eve.

clue.text: Meat dish rises with cooking

indicators.note: cooking the books means falsifying, so these letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A meaty meal that swells up as it cooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link word but is part of the letters RISES WITH that 'cooking' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew of mutton or lamb with potatoes and onions is a traditional Irish meat dish.

clue.text: Got your own back?

parts.note: reclaiming something you had pawned, buying back your own goods, rather than taking revenge

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone has taken revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got your own back' is an idiom for revenge, but read literally it is recovering your own property from a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: To buy back a pawned item is to recover it from the pawnshop, the literal sense of getting one's own back.

clue.text: He breaks more than one union law

definitions.text: He breaks more than one union law

parts.words: He breaks more than one union law
parts.note: a man with more than one wife at once breaks the law on marriage unions

explanation.surface: A trade unionist who flouts several union rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union, but means a marriage; the law broken is the one allowing a single spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who marries while already married commits a crime by having more than one marriage.

clue.text: They're assumed to raise sail in rough sea

indicators.note: the raised sail word sits in the middle of the rearranged sea letters
a rough sea is churned up, so its letters are rearranged
in a down clue, raising something sends it upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors are expected to hoist the sail in heavy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to raise' reads upwards; 'rough' gives AES, which 'in' splits around the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: False names are adopted, that is, taken on or assumed, to hide one's identity.

clue.text: Unable to sleep, due to ship's movement?

definitions.meaning: lying awake turning restlessly in bed, as in turning and twisting all night
a vessel pitching and rolling about on the waves

explanation.surface: A sailor kept awake by the rolling of the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes restless turning in bed and also a ship being thrown about in heavy seas.

clue.text: Property gets one thousand short of estimate

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so the letters for a thousand are missing

parts.note: taken as written
I is one and M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A building valued a thousand pounds below its estimate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes I and M from ESTIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A landed holding, such as a country house with its grounds, is a piece of property.

clue.text: Oil change needed after journey in capital

indicators.note: the rearranged oil letters come after the journey word

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: a change of order means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A car's oil needs replacing after a long drive in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' suggests an oil change; it is the anagram signal, and 'after' sets its result behind the journey word.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief city of Libya, on the Mediterranean coast, is the seat of its government.

clue.text: Joys of French windows

parts.note: de is the French word for of
lights is an old word for windows or panes of glass

explanation.surface: The pleasures of French windows, the glazed doors opening onto a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French windows' looks like one phrase; 'of French' gives DE and 'windows' gives LIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasures and things that give great happiness are both joys, used here as a plural noun.

clue.text: Father tries moving piano first

indicators.note: the piano letter is placed first, before the rest

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for soft

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about, so these are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dad attempts to shift a piano, starting with it before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like shifting furniture but is the anagram signal; 'first' places the piano letter at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic and Anglican clergy are addressed as Father, so a clergyman is one.

clue.text: It sounds like the height of irritation

indicators.note: the clue says the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a peak is the highest point, the height of something

explanation.surface: A remark that some noise is extremely annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the height of irritation' reads as one phrase; 'height' gives the sound and 'irritation' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit of resentment or wounded pride is a kind of irritation or annoyance.

clue.text: Woolly lot of wild geese

definitions.meaning: a coiled length of wool or yarn
the collective noun for a flight of wild geese in the air

explanation.surface: A vague, muddled flock of wild birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolly' looks like fuzzy-minded but means made of wool; the same word names a flock of geese in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a loosely coiled length of yarn and also the collective term for geese flying.

clue.text: Take a chance injecting dope in dog

indicators.note: the gamble word has the fool synonym put into it, as a needle injects

parts.note: to bet is to take a chance on something
a dope is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: Doping a racing dog, a gamble on the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests drugs but means an idiot; 'injecting' puts ASS into BET.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged hound with long ears, bred for tracking hares, is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Sort of question found in inverted commas

indicators.note: to sort something is to rearrange it, so the following word is reordered

explanation.surface: A type of query that appears within quotation marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like 'kind of' but rearranges QUESTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverted commas are the British name for quotation marks, so words inside them are quoted.

clue.text: Burden of love to star making a comeback

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: a comeback returns, so the star word is read backwards

parts.note: the sun is our nearest star

explanation.surface: A star returning to the stage carries the weight of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests a performer, and 'comeback' a return to the stage; here the star is our sun, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Responsibility or obligation that weighs on someone is a burden, as in the burden of proof.

clue.text: Wearing an outfit, like a dramatic opera singer?

indicators.note: to outfit is to rig out afresh, so these letters are re-dressed in a new order

explanation.surface: A performer in costume, larger than life on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outfit' reads as clothing but rearranges WEARING AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand, heroic and on a vast scale, in the style of the composer of the Ring cycle, whose singers are famously powerful.
